issues.legal_issue: A transferor’s claim that an executed deed was procured by misrepresentation fails when the evidence does not establish that the transferor was misled about the nature of the document.
material_facts: The transferor alleged that he signed the deed believing it to be a power of attorney for managing the properties.
He was capable of managing his affairs, took the draft to his own lawyer for advice, and presented the deed for registration himself.
After execution, he did not seek accounts or enquire how the properties were managed.
In an earlier proceeding, he argued that the deed did not pass title but did not claim that it had been procured by misrepresentation.
The court accepted the opposing witnesses’ testimony and found the transferor had not proved misrepresentation.
issues.conclusion: The deed was not vitiated by misrepresentation, and the transferor’s claim to set it aside on that ground failed.
issues.legal_principle: The person alleging misrepresentation bears the burden of proving it. The court applied that burden to the evidence of the transferor’s understanding, conduct, and actions surrounding execution; no statute or earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: suit_to_set_aside_deed_for_misrepresentation and (execution_after_independent_legal_advice and personally_presented_for_registration) and (post_execution_conduct_consistent_with_transfer or no_earlier_misrepresentation_claim)

predicates.suit_to_set_aside_deed_for_misrepresenta: A party brought a suit seeking to set aside an executed deed on the ground that it was procured by misrepresentation.
predicates.execution_after_independent_legal_advice: The transferor obtained independent legal advice about the draft before executing the deed.
predicates.personally_presented_for_registration: The transferor personally presented the executed deed for registration.
predicates.post_execution_conduct_consistent_with_t: After execution, the transferor did not seek accounts or enquire about the management of the transferred property.
predicates.no_earlier_misrepresentation_claim: In an earlier proceeding concerning the deed, the transferor challenged its effect without alleging that it had been procured by misrepresentation.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to set aside a deed for misrepresentation, obtaining independent legal advice and acting consistently with the transfer, or not raising misrepresentation in an earlier challenge, supports the output that misrepresentation was not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A registered instrument without consideration can operate as a gift when it clearly shows an intention to transfer property and is signed by the donor and attested by at least two witnesses.
material_facts: The deed was registered and signed by the transferor.
It stated that the transferor owned the properties and used operative words conveying the properties and associated rights to the recipients.
The deed expressly stated that no consideration had been received.
The deed was attested by more than two witnesses.
issues.conclusion: The deed operated as a gift and effectively transferred title.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a gift may be effected by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor and attested by at least two witnesses. A registered release instrument without consideration operates as a gift if it clearly shows an intention to transfer title and satisfies those formal requirements. The court followed T. Mammo v. K. Ramunni on the requirement that the document disclose an intention to effect a transfer.

rule.if: registered_transfer_instrument and no_consideration and clear_intention_to_transfer and signed_by_donor and attested_by_at_least_two_witnesses

predicates.registered_transfer_instrument: The instrument transferring the property was registered.
predicates.no_consideration: The transferor received no consideration for the transfer.
predicates.clear_intention_to_transfer: The instrument’s terms clearly showed that the transferor intended to convey ownership to the recipient.
predicates.attested_by_at_least_two_witnesses: At least two witnesses attested the instrument.

issues.definition: A registered transfer instrument expressing an intention to transfer property without consideration effectively transfers title as a gift when the donor signs it and at least two witnesses attest it.

issues.legal_issue: An instrument described as a release deed can transfer ownership to a recipient who had no prior interest in the property if its operative words sufficiently express an intention to transfer title.
material_facts: The recipients had no interest in the properties before execution of the deed.
The deed described the transferor as owner and its operative words conveyed the properties and associated rights to the recipients.
The deed was intended to transfer ownership, rather than merely enlarge an existing limited interest.
issues.conclusion: The deed transferred ownership to recipients who had no prior interest in the properties.
issues.legal_principle: The legal effect of an instrument depends on its operative words and intended effect, not merely on its description as a release deed. A release can transfer title to a person who previously had no interest if its words are sufficiently broad. Hutchi Gowder v. Bheema Gowder and S. P. Chinnathambiar v. V. R. P. Chinnathambiar were distinguished: neither established that a document styled as a release could never transfer title to a person without a prior interest.

rule.if: instrument_styled_as_release and recipient_had_no_prior_interest and operative_words_sufficiently_convey_title and intention_to_transfer_ownership

predicates.instrument_styled_as_release: The instrument was described as a release deed.
predicates.recipient_had_no_prior_interest: The recipient had no interest in the property before the instrument was executed.
predicates.operative_words_sufficiently_convey_titl: The instrument’s operative words were broad enough to convey ownership to the recipient.
predicates.intention_to_transfer_ownership: The instrument was intended to transfer ownership rather than merely enlarge an existing interest.

issues.definition: A document described as a release deed transfers ownership to a recipient with no prior interest when its operative words sufficiently convey title and it was intended to transfer ownership.

issues.legal_issue: Execution of an attested instrument is sufficiently proved where the executing party admits signing it and the attestation, and there is no showing that the other attesting witnesses were available to be called.
material_facts: Several attesting witnesses to the deed testified at trial.
The executing party admitted in his testimony that he signed the deed and that the witnesses attested it.
There was no showing that the other attesting witnesses were alive or subject to the court’s process during the trial.
The objection that execution had not been proved was not raised in the courts below.
issues.conclusion: The deed was duly proved, and the objection to proof of execution failed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, governs proof of execution of documents required by law to be attested. The court found no force in the objection in light of the admission of execution and attestation and the absence of proof that the other attesting witnesses were available to be called.

predicates.challenge_to_proof_of_attested_instrumen: A party challenged whether an instrument required to be attested had been proved in the proceeding.
predicates.executant_admitted_signature_and_attesta: The person who executed the instrument admitted signing it and admitted that witnesses attested it.
predicates.no_showing_other_attestors_available: There was no showing that the other attesting witnesses were available to be called at trial.

issues.definition: When proof of an attested instrument is challenged, the executing party’s admission of signature and attestation, together with no showing that other attestors were available, supports the output that execution was duly proved.
